question: A compliance stakeholder wants your architecture decision documented for a workload that must keep inference within a specific geography and avoid retaining prompt content. Select the three statements that accurately support this design conversation.
options: A) The inference_geo parameter is only available on Amazon Bedrock and is not supported on the first-party Claude API
B) The inference_geo parameter lets you specify "global" or "us" routing per request, giving you geographic control over where model inference runs
C) Data residency controls determine which Claude model version responds to a request, so specifying "us" routing automatically pins the request to Claude Haiku 4.5
D) Zero Data Retention is available for every feature on the platform without exception, so no further review of specific features is needed once ZDR is enabled account-wide
E) Regional Bedrock and Google Cloud endpoints guarantee data routing through specific geographic regions, as an alternative to the Claude API's inference_geo parameter
F) Data residency is listed as ZDR eligible, so geographic routing can be combined with a zero-data-retention arrangement in the same architecture
correct_answers: B) The inference_geo parameter lets you specify "global" or "us" routing per request, giving you geographic control over where model inference runs
E) Regional Bedrock and Google Cloud endpoints guarantee data routing through specific geographic regions, as an alternative to the Claude API's inference_geo parameter
F) Data residency is listed as ZDR eligible, so geographic routing can be combined with a zero-data-retention arrangement in the same architecture
explanations: Incorrect — inference_geo is available on the Claude API and Claude Platform on AWS, not exclusive to Bedrock.
Correct — the inference_geo parameter lets you specify "global" or "us" routing per request, controlling where inference runs.
Incorrect — geographic routing controls where inference executes, not which model version is selected.

Incorrect — ZDR eligibility is evaluated per feature; features like the Batch API and MCP connector are explicitly Not ZDR eligible, so account-wide enablement does not cover every feature automatically.
Correct — Bedrock and Google Cloud offer regional endpoints that guarantee data routing through specific geographic regions, as an alternative to the Claude API's parameter.
Correct — the data residency feature row lists it as ZDR eligible.
